reason: The electrolysis unit has separate receivers for its gases, so I’ll start by fitting the hydrogen receiver.
expectation: I expect the receiver to be connected to the hydrogen side; oxygen may still need its own receiver before collection begins.

Capturing carbon dioxide is also a goal, but I’ll start with the water electrolysis unit.

effect: The hydrogen receiver is collecting gas already, while oxygen follows a separate circuit. I’ll fit its receiver next.
reaction: I’m a little surprised electrolysis started before the oxygen receiver was fitted.
reason: The oxygen receiver belongs at the same unit and should complete collection of both gases.
expectation: I expect the receiver to collect oxygen from the separate circuit and possibly complete the electrolysis goal.

reaction: The distinction between oxygen as oxidizer and fuel is useful.

expectation: I expect the receiver to collect and compress carbon dioxide, completing that goal.

effect: Carbon dioxide capture completes the chapter’s two goals and provides a compressed ingredient for the plant.
reaction: The idea of gathering a chemical ingredient from the thin Martian air is interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Collecting oxygen was most worthwhile because the result clarified its role as the lander’s oxidizer.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the separate receivers became a little repetitive, although the results distinguished the gases and their roles.

surprise.text: I was surprised that hydrogen began collecting before the oxygen receiver was fitted.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; each receiver matched a named unit and an explicit goal.

continue.text: Yes. I’m curious how the collected gases will support the early return and what happens to the specimens.
